papers.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
papers.abstract: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and

papers.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
papers.abstract: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment
papers.llm_reason: ★ **今日第四即时价值。**（arXiv 2611.08452《ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts》）★ 核心问题（论文全文口径）：复现 ML 实验需要从论文、已发布代码和零散工件里重建过程，**因此对 coding agent 而言，复现成败可能取决于它自己补全缺失细节的能力，而不只取决于已发布的工件**。作者问：**把重建出来的过程与决策保留下来，是否能提升后续的独立复现**。方法 ReproBridge 定义了标准化工件四件套：**refined codebase（精炼代码库）+ environment setup（环境配置）+ experiment launchers（实验启动器）+ reproduction guide（复现指南）**，并实现为一个 agent workflow。★ 实测口径（论文 + 项目页逐条核对）：ReproBridge-Bench 含 **1,029 个任务、来自 36 篇论文的 387 个实验，每个任务锚定 5 个人工核验的参考分数**；**四个模型在 fresh session 里分别用原始代码或精炼工件尝试，独立 Auditor 检查执行证据**；**精炼工件把平均复现成功率从 76.4% 提到 92.6%**，**并把下游 API 花费平均降低 19.7%**；**跨模型成功率离散度从 21.6 个百分点收窄到 3.9 个百分点，四个模型平均成功率全部超过 90%**；**消融显示去掉任一组件都会掉成功率，其中去掉代码与环境损失最大**。★ papers.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
papers.abstract: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. papers.llm_reason: ★ **今日第五价值。**（arXiv 2611.08478《Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists》）★ 核心洞见（论文全文口径）：**「AI-Scientists 来了，但它们长大的世界没有来。」**人类科学家的世界是几个世纪的开放问题 + 共享想法 + 科学文献；对 AI-Scientist 来说这个世界 **readable but not runnable（可读但不可运行）**。Scientist World 的做法是：**每一篇研究论文都变成一个可执行环境**——自动流水线从每篇论文里抽出开放式研究问题，并把论文提出的方法复现成 baseline；进入该环境的 AI-Scientist **以「作者本人做到什么程度」为被评测对象**。★ 实测口径（论文全文口径，逐条核对）：**发布首批 1,000 个已验证环境**；**用这个世界当评测，前沿 AI-Scientist 已能在 74% 的时间里超过人类研究者**；**包含 6,400 小时研究轨迹（每一个想法、实验、失败与成功）**；**作为训练场，能把一个小模型提升 +158% 使其在研究构想能力上追平前沿模型**。全文 §F.1 与 Figure 35 进一步拆开：**在 But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains.
